0|97b8ee845393701edc06e27ccec2876ff9596019|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"ring-buffer: Fix polling on trace_pipe
ring_buffer_poll_wait() should always put the poll_table to its wait_queue
even there is immediate data available.  Otherwise
read sequence will eventually hang forever:
1. Put some data to make the trace_pipe ring_buffer read ready first
2. epoll_ctl(efd
3. epoll_wait()
4. read(trace_pipe_fd) till EAGAIN
5. Add some more data to the trace_pipe ring_buffer
6. epoll_wait() -> this epoll_wait() will block forever
~ During the epoll_ctl(efd
ring_buffer_poll_wait() returns immediately without adding poll_table
which has poll_table->_qproc pointing to ep_poll_callback()
wait_queue.
~ During the epoll_wait() call in step 3 and step 6
ring_buffer_poll_wait() cannot add ep_poll_callback() to its wait_queue
because the poll_table->_qproc is NULL and it is how epoll works.
~ When there is new data available in step 6
it has to call ep_poll_callback() because it is not in its wait queue.
Hence
Other poll implementation seems to call poll_wait() unconditionally as the very
first thing to do.  For example
